I really did not expect this level of response from you Voaters to my theme. Cashmere has gotten a lot of praise and constructive criticism, both of which I greatly appreciate. I've also received a lot of questions about how to do this or that. I'm trying to answer all of these, and I've managed to keep up so far, but it has limited my ability to continue development at the rate I'd like or talk about the goals of this project. In this post, I'm just going to put down a bunch of thoughts I have because I want to communicate about where this is heading.

First, I want you to understand my technical abilities:

I've been working with CSS for a few years and I think I'm pretty good with it, however, this is the first Sass project I have released and I had never used Git or GitHub. Git/Hub has been a big learning curve for me. Just today, I made some changes I didn't like and wanted to revert my local working directory back to the latest commit, but I haven't figured it out yet. I also suck at versioning my software, as this is also new for me. When I released the code last Sunday, I decided that was version 1.0, but as I keep updating it, the version hasn't changed. That's not terribly useful. All I know is Cashmere is currently one-point-something.

Short-term goals:

These are some things I've been planning to deal with since I published and haven't properly had a chance to.

Styling the modal dialogs (things that pop up, such as the log-in box). They just don't mesh with the rest of the style. I have some additional CSS applied to them, but I'm not happy with the result yet.

The margins are also inconsistent on a number of elements and I need to put more relevant information on the sidebar.

Mid-term goals:

After I get the basics tweaked so everything is cleaner, I'm going to implement more features. People have asked about sidebar and banner images and these are both things I will get around to. Cashmere also has accessibility issues I will address at this point. Being able to operate a web page without a mouse is crucial for some people. Currently, I have a couple elements which cannot be accessed without a mouse, including the log-out button, which is pretty damn important.

Long-term ideas:

I won't even call these "goals" at this point, but they are things I have considered. Getting Cashmere to work across all of Voat is something a few people have asked about. This could be in the form of a browser extension or implemented by the admins (I have control over one of these things). As it stands, Voat has many pages which Cashmere is not currently capable of dealing with, so it can't simply be plugged in. I may eventually extend the theme in this way, but that's currently outside the scope of the project. I need to focus on making Cashmere as good as I can make it for the use of moderators who want to apply it to their subverses -- then I can decide whether to broaden the scope to include the entirety of Voat somehow.

I would also like to make Cashmere seriously easy to customize -- I'm thinking about some sort of web interface which someone who has never written a line of CSS in their life could use. Again, this is not something I will work on until I'm satisfied that the short-to-mid-term goals have been satisfied.

What you can do:

Keep reporting bugs. I know there are a few. If something looks broken, make a submission and explain the issue, give your OS and browser details, and ideally add a screenshot.

If you have used successfully used Sass to process the SCSS, I would like to know how it went. I plan on posting a beginner's guide, but I have a limited ability to experiment under different operating systems, particularly Windows.

TL;DR:

First, I'm completing the things that were always considered to be works-in-progress. Then I will implement additional features. Then -- I don't really know -- but I have some rough ideas about how this project could continue to flourish.

 

Thank you for your interest in Cashmere, especially if you read this entire post!

Hey! Let me know if you have git or GitHub specific questions. The GitHub desktop app is pretty good for the basics of committing and pushing but you’ll sometimes need the command line for more esoteric operations.

I wouldn’t worry too much about versions. The lazy way I handle smaller projects is to tag releases by date (effectively using dates as versions). Or you can bump the version number for “stable” releases only, and just commit minor changes without changing the version. If people need to talk about specific “in between” versions they can use the commit hash.

Also, if you’re getting a lot of questions about CSS not specific to your theme, feel free to direct them to /v/CustomizingVoat or /v/CSS. We’re here to help.
